title: Manager contract — one page replacing ~6,200 lines of process skills
note: DONE in this PR: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. One job, one register, spawn rules, model table, budget, brief format. landed_unproven until a manager session is observed running against it. [!] Shipped in PR #12668 (3ea2777). Still `landed_unproven`: merged is not observed, and for the doc rows the observation that matters is whether a SESSION can actually work from them -- which the next manager session is the first test of. [!] THE TEST WAS RUN, 2026-09-21/22. VERDICT: WORKABLE, WITH ONE NAMED GAP. The contract was invoked at session start and held all day -- the may-not-take-an-item rule, the spawn model and the provenance requirement all did real work, and the one time the manager did take an item (B2) the contract's own escape hatch forced the reasoning to be written down rather than assumed. ⚠️ THE GAP: IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A LANE THAT CANNOT COMMIT. Three lanes on one four-line task ended without a single commit, blocked on interactive Bash approvals; the contract has no instruction for the manager at that point, and the manager improvised (re-dispatch twice, then take it under exception). Whatever the right answer is, the contract should carry it. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS a later manager session reporting the same, independently. CLOSED 2026-09-25: multiple manager sessions since the original test (09-22 through 09-25, confirmed via git log on MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json) have run continuously against .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md, and the named gap (a lane that cannot commit) recurred on 2026-09-24 (lane B5, blocked on a Claude Code permission prompt) and was folded into the contract itself rather than improvised again -- independent, later confirmation the contract works, satisfying this row's close condition.
